column1: # policy/ops/ops-sandbox.tsv — THE OPERATOR'S PER-TOOL SANDBOX TABLE (S2/S3).
# THE AUTHOR IS THE OPERATOR, exactly like ops-aliases.tsv and ops-hosts.tsv.
# This table lets the operator TIGHTEN a host tool's sandbox below its
# DECLARED set — which is the executor's BASELINE plus the tool's SIDECAR (a
# file next to its program binary declaring what it needs beyond the baseline).
# It is the palisade half of "configure the sandbox by policy": the proxy is
# the only process at the spawn, it already evaluates this operator policy
# in-process, and the pin (policy/ops/PINS) makes every edit a visible release
# — a per-generation Dhall spec would be invisible to the per-boot record, so
# datalog/ops policy owns the spec and Dhall has no role in v1 (do not re-open
# that decision).
# Columns (TAB-separated; '#' starts a comment):
#   tool        a HOST TOOL name (one of the proxy's pinned registry names —
#               host_time, host_cat).  An unknown tool is a STARTUP REFUSAL
#               naming the row.
#   promises    the tool's pledge tokens, space-separated, from the 23-token
#               cosmocc vocabulary (stdio rpath wpath cpath dpath flock fattr
#               inet unix dns tty recvfd proc exec id unveil sendfd settime
#               prot_exec vminfo tmppath chown anet).
#   landlock    "path:perms;path:perms;..." — the operator's ALLOWLIST of the
#               paths the tool may unveil beyond its static spec (the baseline
#               loader + libc + the sidecar's own paths, which the spawn always
#               adds).  perms is an unveil perm string over {r,w,x,c}.
# SILENCE = THE TOOL'S OWN DECLARATION.  A tool with NO row here runs under
# its DECLARED set — the baseline + its sidecar, or the baseline alone if it
# declares no sidecar.  There is NO "unsandboxed" state: every spawn is
# wrapped in stage3, and a tool that needs MORE than it declared FAILS LOUDLY
# on its first attempt instead of silently running bare.  This table's shipped
# state is the declaration for every tool (no rows), and the restriction a
# host tool actually faces is the declared set PLUS the operator's alias class
# table (D3 + the totality check).
# DENY-MORE-ONLY, IN BOTH DIMENSIONS, ENFORCED AT THE SEAT (not just stated):
#   * promises — the row's tokens must be a SUBSET of the tool's DECLARED set
#     (baseline + sidecar).  A token beyond the declared set is a STARTUP
#     REFUSAL naming the row and the token (never a silent widening).  The row
#     may also not drop `stdio` or `exec` (the baseline's own self-check: a
#     set without exec kills every call, one without stdio breaks the program
#     contract).
#   * landlock — the row's allowlist can only NARROW which paths the tool may
#     read: the spawn unveils EXACTLY the per-call judged path `:r` (and never
#     a path the call did not name), and only when that path appears in the
#     row's allowlist.  A path dropped from the row makes the call's open fail
#     EACCES while the alias table still judges the call allowed.  A perm wider
#     than the per-call `r` is a STARTUP REFUSAL naming the row.
# RLIMITS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT HERE.  stage3's resource limits (RATTAN_RLIMITS)
# are a compiled-in executor field, not an operator lever: deny-more-only for
# rlimits is awkward and the operator has no business tuning them.
# ONE SPELLING.  The AUTHORITATIVE check of this table is the SEAT's own
# subset composition (tools/fx-hostgate.c: ops_load_sandbox, run at startup,
# before the slave path is published) against the DECLARED set the sidecar
# loader (fh_sandbox_load) composed.  policy/ops/eval_ops.py's --check-sandbox
# is GRAMMAR ONLY — the promise-token vocabulary, the landlock perm grammar,
# the tool-name charset — and it NEVER re-spells the declared set: the seat is
# the single source, so a sidecar edit and the python check can never drift
# into two different vocabularies.
# The table is pinned in policy/ops/PINS: editing it is a re-pin (a release),
# artifact + PINS in the SAME commit.
# The shipped state is the DECLARATION (no rows).  To narrow host_cat to a
# specific readable set, add a row (the example below is commented out):
# host_cat
